hoses: Supply line from hydrant to Engine 181 intake
100 ft of 2½-inch hose from Engine 181 discharge to FDC
150 ft of 2½-inch attack line from standpipe outlet to nozzle

problems.title: Sixth-Floor Standpipe Elevation
problems.question: The standpipe attack is operating on the 6th floor. For this training problem, use height = (floor number - 1) × 10 ft and the fireground approximation elevation pressure = height × 0.5 PSI/ft. What elevation pressure must be added?
formulaBreakdown: 6th floor is 5 floors above the 1st floor.
problems.instructorExplanation: Use the number of floors above the first floor, then multiply by 10 ft and the stated 0.5 PSI/ft training approximation.
problems.explainMistake: Do not label this value as standpipe system loss. It is the elevation-pressure component only.

problems.title: Elevation Pressure Change
problems.question: The attack is operating from the 5th floor. For this training problem, use height = (floor number - 1) × 10 ft and elevation pressure = height × 0.5 PSI/ft. What elevation pressure must be added?
problems.instructorExplanation: The 5th floor is treated as 40 ft above grade in this training convention, producing a 20 PSI elevation allowance.
problems.explainMistake: Do not count the 1st floor as 10 ft of elevation in this scenario.

problems.title: Total Pump Discharge Pressure
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying a 5th-floor standpipe operation through 100 ft of 2½-inch hose to the FDC and 150 ft of 2½-inch attack hose from the outlet to a 1⅛-inch smooth bore nozzle flowing 265 GPM at 50 PSI. For this training problem, use 20 PSI elevation to the 5th floor and assume a 25 PSI standpipe/FDC system loss. What pump discharge pressure is required?
formulaBreakdown: FDC supply hose FL = 2 × (265 / 100)^2 × 1 ≈ 14 PSI, rounded to 15 PSI.
Interior attack-line FL = 2 × (265 / 100)^2 × 1.5 ≈ 21 PSI, rounded to 20 PSI.
problems.instructorExplanation: For this scenario, include the FDC supply hose, interior attack hose, nozzle pressure, stated elevation allowance, and the explicitly assumed 25 PSI system loss.
problems.explainMistake: Do not treat 25 PSI as a universal standpipe loss; it is an assumption stated for this training scenario.
